persons.name: Leslie
persons.harm: Over about four months in 2010, her online-dating boyfriend love-bombed, lied to, gaslit and controlled her, cut her off from her family (especially her sister), and moved into her house. On the first night she left her adopted son alone with him, he fatally beat the boy.

quotes.quote: If I ever confronted him about anything throughout our relationship, by the end of the conversation, I would feel guilty about ever even doubting him. Gaslighting at its finest.
As it was right now, I could not afford to make it in this house without him. I couldn't afford the mortgage on my own.
I never thought he would hurt me or Jace, but I was afraid he would threaten to kill himself and he would never leave me alone.

contacts.institution: Tulsa Police Department (patrol officers, then a Child Crisis Unit detective)
contacts.when: morning of June 13, 2010, at the hospital, and repeatedly during the investigation
contacts.what_was_asked: Police came to the hospital about the child's injuries. Leslie gave her account of the relationship and of the injuries.
contacts.what_institution_did: The detective interviewed her several times, concluded she was not involved and had been manipulated, and told the family the boyfriend was a sociopath who had tricked her.
contacts.quote: And then when I met Leslie, my gut was like, okay, I really don't think she's involved. It seems like she really was taking steps to try to figure out and get to the bottom of these injuries, but somehow he kind of fell through the cracks, honestly.
contacts.what_happened_next: The investigation led to an arrest warrant and his arrest 10 days later. Leslie says the lead detective 'was the only one who finally helped me accept that [perpetrator] did this.'
contacts.notes: Stacey corroborates: 'But the police all acknowledged like, no, this is a sociopath. He is a bad guy that tricked you.' (s17-e3-living-in-a-nightmare @ 45:17). Leslie: 'She did her job well and treated everyone with respect.' (@ 31:54).

contacts.institution: Oklahoma Department of Human Services / Child Protective Services, acting with the Tulsa PD detective
contacts.when: June 13, 2010, about two days before a judge let her back
contacts.what_was_asked: Leslie wanted to be with her dying son in hospital.
contacts.what_institution_did: Jace was placed in protective custody and Leslie was removed and barred from the hospital, because she was one of only two adults caring for him during the period when the injury happened.
contacts.quote: They wouldn't allow Leslie to be at the hospital. The Department of Human Services, Child Protective Services was involved, so they wouldn't allow her to be at the hospital.
contacts.what_happened_next: She went before a judge two days later and was allowed back.
contacts.notes: The detective: 'So I had to place Jason protective custody. So I basically had to kick Leslie out of the hospital and make her leave' (@ 24:46-25:46). She also says she did not personally suspect Leslie, so this was protocol rather than an accusation. I coded it as treating Leslie as a suspect and excluding her (a punitive effect), and noted that it could also be read as a procedural step. Leslie's best friend: 'they have to question her. Did you know about this? Really making her feel like a crappy parent?' (@ 15:29).

contacts.institution: a judge (court hearing on the DHS custody)
contacts.what_was_asked: To be allowed to be at the hospital with Jace.
contacts.what_institution_did: The judge allowed her to be at the hospital.
contacts.quote: She had to go before a judge two days later and the judge then allowed her to be at the hospital.
contacts.what_happened_next: She was with Jace before life support was withdrawn and his organs were donated. He died on June 16, 2010.
contacts.notes: Stacey's account.

contacts.when: months after Jace's death, before the trial
contacts.what_was_asked: Counseling after the murder.
contacts.what_institution_did: The counselor told her the perpetrator was responsible, not her.
contacts.quote: But the police all acknowledged like, no, this is a sociopath. He is a bad guy that tricked you. That helped me to hear that. Leslie's counselor that she went to said the same thing.
contacts.what_happened_next: Leslie later describes years of therapy and working through her guilt.
contacts.notes: Stacey's account. The quote continues across the 46:23 timestamp.

contacts.institution: Tulsa County District Attorney's Office (crimes-against-children prosecutors)
contacts.what_was_asked: Leslie gave her account and printed out all her text messages with the perpetrator for the prosecution.
contacts.what_institution_did: The prosecutors supported the family, used her texts as trial evidence, and treated the boyfriend as the guilty party, not her.
contacts.quote: The DA did her job well and treated everyone with respect. She never came at us with accusations. Sure, she thought I should have made better decisions, joined the club. But she knew who the guilty party was.
contacts.what_happened_next: The case went to trial in February 2012.
contacts.notes: Leslie recalls one moment when 'I felt like I could sense her questioning my motives' about why she printed the texts (@ 4:11-5:14). The DA also told her she didn't think a suit against the ER doctor would succeed (s17-e4-pure-evil @ 44:29). Stacey says the family refused a plea deal (s17-e3 @ 46:23).

contacts.institution: Tulsa County District Attorney's Office (closing argument at trial)
contacts.what_was_asked: Nothing; this was the prosecution's closing argument.
contacts.what_institution_did: In open court, the prosecutor called Leslie the 'biggest what if', said she had been foolish and negligent as a single parent, and told the jury they could be angry at her while still convicting him.
contacts.quote: Probably the biggest what if in this case is Leslie. How could somebody so smart be so dumb?
contacts.what_happened_next: The jury convicted. Leslie: 'That was very hard to hear, but it was also true.' (@ 22:24)
contacts.notes: This is read from the trial transcript. The DA had warned her beforehand that 'she will have to say things about me' (@ 17:20). The argument was rhetorical, meant to head off jurors' anger at the mother, and ends with 'But does that mean he's not responsible?' Coded blamed because the passage directly assigns fault to Leslie in public. I did not treat it as an accusation of a crime.

contacts.what_was_asked: Conviction for child abuse murder in the first degree.
contacts.what_institution_did: The jury found him guilty and fixed punishment at life and a $10,000 fine.
contacts.quote: The defendant is guilty and fixed punishment at life and a fine of $10,000.
contacts.what_happened_next: Sentencing in April 2012: life with the possibility of parole, because one juror would not agree to life without parole. Leslie gave a victim impact statement.
contacts.notes: The judge did not let Stacey's or the earlier child's written victim impact statements be read aloud, though Leslie and her mother read theirs (s17-e5-verdict @ 31:35).

contacts.what_was_asked: The perpetrator sought release and appealed. The family wanted the conviction upheld.
contacts.what_institution_did: Denied both appeals and at least three post-conviction requests.
contacts.quote: He tried that at least three times, which was denied by the judge. He tried two appeals, which were denied, and he has no other options.
contacts.what_happened_next: He remains in prison. Leslie says he must serve at least 38 years before parole is considered.
contacts.notes: Stacey says she checked the court dockets herself (s17-e5-verdict @ 44:00). She is a family member, not the show, so 'record_checked_by_show' is loosely applied here.

persons.outcome_quote: You have been found guilty and will spend the rest of your life in prison. A sentence I believe is too easy on you for what you really deserve, but I take solace and knowing you will never have the opportunity to hurt another child. Never be able to manipulate and control another woman
persons.decisive_work_quote: After Chase died, of course, we had to wait for the autopsy to get the official calls of death. Short time after that, I typed up an arrest warrant. I presented it to the District Attorney's Office and they issued a warrant for his arrest for first degree murder.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: same day the harm first reached an institution (June 13, 2010); arrest 10 days later; conviction about 20 months later
persons.notes: Her own harm (coercive control and manipulation) reached an institution only through the investigation of her son's fatal injury. I coded 'protected' because the investigation, arrest and conviction ended the perpetrator's access to her, after earlier institutional harm (her exclusion from the hospital, and the prosecutor's public blame in closing). A reader could reasonably code 'partly_protected' instead: the gravest harm, her son's murder, came before any institution acted for her, and his family's harassment continued, including online forum posts accusing her and Stacey (s17-e3 @ 43:15-45:17) and his sister's messages years later (s17-ep6-healer @ 34:09-38:16). Those are separate actors and never reached an institution, so I gave them no separate record. The never-reached reasons explain why she stayed and did not act sooner, not a decision to avoid reporting. Contributors: Stacey told patrol officers about his history; Leslie printed her texts and testified; the earlier child's mother ('Samantha') testified.

persons.name: Jace
persons.harm: Leslie's adopted son, aged 2-3, was repeatedly physically abused (bilateral ear bruising, marks on his wrists, shaking) by his mother's boyfriend from about March to June 2010. On the night of June 12-13, 2010 he suffered fatal blunt-force head trauma in the boyfriend's sole care, and he died June 16, 2010.

quotes.quote: There is no way the man I loved and saw daily how much he loved and cared for Chase could ever hurt him when I wasn't around. I couldn't even entertain that thought.

When you think about calling in an allegation of child abuse and reporting that, I would hope that if every single one of us would say that if we suspect it, we would call it in. But when you're talking about your own family, it makes it a little bit more difficult.

contacts.institution: emergency room at the hospital where Leslie worked (ER physician)
contacts.when: spring 2010, the night bruising appeared inside both ears after a day in the boyfriend's care
contacts.what_was_asked: Leslie, his mother, brought him in on a nurse practitioner's advice, worried about a skull fracture.
contacts.what_institution_did: The physician saw nothing urgent and offered a CT only if she wanted one. In the chart he wrote that the bruising looked like the child had been slapped on both sides of the head, but he made no DHS or social-work referral and left follow-up to the pediatrician.
contacts.quote: Later, I would find out he documented in his notes in the official legal chart that it appeared to be child abuse, like someone slapped Jace on both sides of his head. but there was no social worker on site during the night, so he would let the pediatrician follow up.
contacts.what_happened_next: They saw the pediatrician the next day. No report was made.
contacts.notes: Leslie reads the chart note on air: 'it would appear like the patient was slapped simultaneously on bilateral sides of the head... at 1.30 a.m., it's difficult to engage the Department of Human Services' (s17-e4-pure-evil @ 44:29). The prosecutor's closing asks 'What if the ER doctor had called in a referral' (s17-e5-verdict @ 20:22). The DA advised that a suit would likely fail, and Leslie did not sue (s17-e4 @ 44:29-45:31).

contacts.when: the day after the ER visit, spring 2010
contacts.what_was_asked: Leslie wanted the ear bruising explained. Stacey, who suspected abuse, had pressed Leslie to take him.
contacts.what_institution_did: The pediatrician tested only for a bleeding disorder, which was ruled out, and said to watch it. Abuse was not raised and no report was made. Stacey says the pediatricians 'weren't worried about it.'
contacts.quote: The only reasonable explanation they could come up with was some kind of bleeding disorder. We did testing for that, it was ruled out. We would just have to watch it.
contacts.what_happened_next: The abuse continued. Jace told Stacey the boyfriend 'did it' and later that he 'shook' him.
contacts.notes: Stacey: 'I made my sister take him to the doctor... But the pediatricians said they weren't worried about it.' (s17-e2-be-very-concerned @ 32:01). The detective: 'They took him to the doctor, and they pretty much got dismissed.' (s17-e3 @ 27:50). The bleeding-disorder test was a concrete step but did not address abuse. This could also be coded 'disbelieved' (the abuse concern was dismissed), but the passage does not show abuse being put to the doctor and rejected, so I chose did_nothing_or_delayed. The boyfriend was present: '[perpetrator] was with us. He was always with us.'

contacts.when: a few weeks after the pediatrician visit, at an unrelated follow-up
contacts.what_was_asked: Leslie raised the ear bruising.
contacts.what_institution_did: The ENT suggested he might be sleeping on his ears wrong. Abuse was not raised.
contacts.quote: I brought up the bruising, thinking he might have some insight. Stop, maybe he was sleeping on his ears wrong. No one brought up child abuse.
contacts.what_happened_next: The abuse continued until the fatal injury on June 12-13, 2010.
contacts.notes: Leslie: 'We saw multiple healthcare professionals looking at Jesus's ears and no one took action.' (s17-e4-pure-evil @ 43:28). The detective says the doctors 'regret decisions that they made sending Jason. back home. They testified to that.' (s17-ep6-healer @ 7:13).

contacts.institution: 911 / Tulsa Fire Department first responders and St. Francis Hospital (ER, neurosurgery)
contacts.what_was_asked: Emergency care. The perpetrator called 911 and said the child had fallen out of his toddler bed.
contacts.what_institution_did: Responders rushed him to hospital. Doctors performed emergency brain surgery, recognised that the injuries were not from a fall, and called law enforcement.
contacts.quote: As soon as Jace shows up at the hospital with his massive brain injury and covered in bruises, of course, law enforcement is called.
contacts.what_happened_next: Police and detectives arrived. He was declared brain dead and taken off life support, his organs were donated, and he died June 16, 2010.
contacts.notes: initiated_by is 'third_party' only because the caller was the perpetrator himself. Stacey: 'the nurses communicated basically that this wouldn't happen from just falling off the bed.' (s17-e3 @ 11:23). The quote is from the prosecutor's opening statement, read from the transcript.

contacts.institution: Tulsa Police Department (patrol officers; Child Crisis Unit detectives)
contacts.what_was_asked: Stacey told the patrol officers of her suspicions and of his history with another child.
contacts.what_institution_did: The officers brought in detectives. They interviewed Stacey, Leslie and the boyfriend, photographed and measured the scene and the injuries, and built the timeline that showed he was alone with Jace.
contacts.quote: I say, I have a lot of concerns that [perpetrator] has done something to Jason. And I told him about his history with the other child. And that he was the one that was alone with him. They say, yeah, we were kind of wondering about that, and we'll have the detectives talk to you as soon as they get here.
contacts.what_happened_next: An arrest warrant followed the autopsy.
contacts.notes: The detective describes the investigation (s17-e3 @ 21:40-27:50). Leslie: 'She took pictures of my house... She took measurements of the furniture in Jace's room' (@ 31:54).

contacts.what_was_asked: Nothing; the detective acted on the suspected abuse.
contacts.what_institution_did: Placed the dying child in protective custody.
contacts.quote: So I had to place Jason protective custody.
contacts.what_happened_next: He died June 16, 2010. Custody could no longer protect him.
contacts.notes: The same act excluded Leslie from the hospital (see P01 contact 2).

contacts.institution: Tulsa County District Attorney's Office; Payne County deputies made the arrest
contacts.what_was_asked: The detective presented an arrest warrant.
contacts.what_institution_did: Issued a first-degree murder warrant. He was arrested near Stillwater on June 23, 2010.
contacts.quote: I typed up an arrest warrant. I presented it to the District Attorney's Office and they issued a warrant for his arrest for first degree murder.
contacts.what_happened_next: He stayed in jail until trial. The ADA obtained the 2002 police and DHS records on the earlier child.
contacts.notes: News clips read on air report the arrest (s17-e3 @ 40:12-41:12).

contacts.what_was_asked: Conviction for child abuse murder in the first degree.
contacts.what_institution_did: Guilty verdict. The jury fixed punishment at life and a $10,000 fine.
contacts.quote: The defendant is guilty and fixed punishment at life and a fine of $10,000.
contacts.what_happened_next: Sentencing in April 2012.

contacts.what_was_asked: Sentencing. The family wanted life without parole.
contacts.what_institution_did: The judge imposed life with the possibility of parole, as the jury suggested, because one juror would not agree to life without parole.
contacts.quote: They suggested the sentence of life in prison with the possibility of parole, so that's what the judge did.
contacts.what_happened_next: Minimum of 38 years before parole is considered. Two appeals and at least three post-conviction requests were denied (s17-ep6-healer @ 39:17).

persons.outcome_quote: I really believe something could have maybe changed the outcome of this case if somebody would have just listened to them, he ended up getting murdered before anybody really listened.
persons.notes: He died from the harm, so under the rules the later arrest and conviction are recorded as contacts but are not protection. Three medical contacts before the fatal injury produced no report. I kept harmed_by_institution_ever false because the doctors failed to act (coded did_nothing_or_delayed) rather than actively endangering him; a reader could argue that the ER physician, who wrote that the injury looked like abuse and still sent him home without a referral, endangered him. The season does not say exactly how many separate ear-bruising episodes there were (the prosecutor: 'If you count the first time, Jason's ears were bruised three times'). Stacey's pediatrician account and Leslie's ER-then-pediatrician account may describe the same episode, so I recorded them as one pediatrician contact. Stacey, a former protective-services worker, never called DHS ('I wish I had called DHS', s17-e4-pure-evil @ 47:36); the second never-reached quote is the prosecutor's explanation of that. He was in CPS custody at birth for unrelated reasons, not coded.

persons.name: [unnamed] infant daughter of the perpetrator's earlier girlfriend ('Samantha')
persons.harm: In 2002-2003, at about five or six months old, she suffered abusive head trauma (old and new subdural bleeds, retinal hemorrhages, skull damage, bruising to her face and ears) while her mother's boyfriend was living with them. She was life-flighted and needed brain surgery, and survived.

because when they kept saying that she was hurt like that, I just thought, you're wrong. There's no way. I'm always around her. I've never seen anybody hurt her.

coder_notes: Season 17 (Something Was Wrong) is the story of Leslie, a NICU nurse, whose adopted son Jace was murdered in 2010 by her boyfriend of about four months, and of her sister Stacey. All four chunk files were read in full to their stated last lines (101, 98, 107, 55). A usage-limit interruption came after s17_03.txt line 50; I resumed at line 51 from my notes, so no lines were skipped. The unassigned INDEX was read. No unassigned episode concerned this story, so none was opened; the season's own Data Points: Child Abuse episode, inside s17_04.txt, holds no personal story. Key pattern: three medical contacts (ER, pediatrician, ENT) saw Jace's ear bruising before his death. The ER physician charted that it looked like abuse but made no referral. The 2002 injury to the earlier child led to no charges against the perpetrator, while that child's mother was charged with failure to protect. Detective, prosecutor and court responses after the fatal injury were strong. In all quotations the perpetrator's name is replaced with [perpetrator]; nothing else was changed. Several minor records (P05-P07, P10) are borderline between a person record and others_mentioned, and are marked low confidence. Speech-to-text variants of names (e.g. Jace/Jase/Jason/Chase) appear in the quotes as transcribed.
